input.question: How do people pirate movies that are currently in theaters?
input.ground_truth: 1. Really really good camcorders. 2. Some digital channels allow you to stream movies before they are released, just hit record button. 3. Copies of movies are sent to various critics or private screenings. Those can be stolen.

Okay! Imagine you have a really cool toy that just came out, and you want to show it to your friends before everyone else has it. But the toy is only at the toy store right now, not in your house.

Some people who are not allowed to take the toy without permission (that’s called stealing), sneak into the toy store when nobody is looking, take a picture or video of the toy, and then send those pictures or videos to other people. They might even try to make a copy of the toy at home and give it to others.

For movies, it’s kind of like that. When a movie is in the theater, it’s not on DVD or streaming yet. Some people sneak in with a small camera or phone and secretly film the movie while it’s playing. Then, they can share that movie online so other people can watch it for free, even though they’re not supposed to.

But that’s not a good thing to do, because the people who made the movie worked very hard and need people to pay to watch it in the theater to help them.
